newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Maradona's manager faces judge on cocaine bust.
newsitem.headline: Maradona's manager faces judge on cocaine bust.

text.p: Argentine soccer idol Diego Maradona's manager Guillermo Coppola went before a judge on Friday to protest his innocence of drug charges in a scandal embarrassing his friends in the government.

The silver-haired and tanned Coppola, sporting a black leather cap, went to court in the town of Dolores 180 miles (300 km) south of Buenos Aires to explain to Judge Hernan Bernasconi the one pound (500 g) of cocaine found in a flower vase in his apartment in a pre-dawn raid on Wednesday.
"Totally innocent," were Coppola's only words as he was pushed through a crowd of near-hysterical reporters into a police car that sped him off to a nearby jail.

Since his arrest on Wednesday night, Coppola, 48, has monopolised local television, left Maradona "very distressed" and forced senior officials to try to play down links between Maradona, Coppola and President Carlos Menem and his private secretary Ramon Hernandez.

Maradona and Coppola were at Menem's Casa Rosada palace the night of his election victory in May 1995 and consoled him over the death of his son Carlitos earlier that year. Coppola and Hernandez, who once worked together as bank clerks, are often photographed together at trendy Buenos Aires nightspots.

It was Coppola who persuaded Menem to make Maradona the figurehead of a government drug-fighting campaign last summer. Maradona, suspended for failing a dope test at the U.S. World Cup in 1994, admitted his drug addiction this year.

"They may have connections with someone but that does not mean they are in with those in power, or have any connections with government," Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan told local radio, acknowledging he had seen Maradona and Coppola "occasionally, some time ago" at Menem's Olivos residence.
Coppola's arrest after seven months of surveillance and phone-taps is the latest in a series of drug scandals to hit Maradona and his manager.

Many Maradona fans blame his drug habit on Coppola, and when Maradona played for Naples, Coppola was charged with peddling cocaine drugs to his teammates. The charges were later dropped. He is also being investigated over the death of a Buenos Aires nightclub owner, shot in the head in early 1994.
